title: Recover only exact verified operational record transactions
statement: The Operational record persistence Module shall recover an explicitly selected current-format transaction only by completing its verified exact prepared candidate or restoring its verified before-state, preserving unknown target states, acknowledged commitment, and available recoverability.

what.problem: A stale or damaged recovery record can cause guessed replacement, replay of old semantic operations, or destruction of outside work.
what.desired_outcome: Recovery produces the selected verified storage state or an explicit safe stop while keeping unrelated content and historical meaning intact.

why.rationale: SR-045 makes recovery an exact byte-preserving transaction operation rather than a new engineering decision or general rollback facility.

stakeholders: Actors resolving an interrupted recorded update
Consumers relying on acknowledged saved results

conditions: The caller explicitly selects restore or complete with the transaction and expected recovery identity.
Recovery is interrupted, repeated, or encounters changed targets or unavailable private data.

contexts: IF-003 recovery of one selected current operational-record transaction.
Its private journal and verified before/candidate snapshots; external decision-basis subjects remain read-only.

how.approach: Validate the supported journal, exact snapshots, current recovery identity, containment, and observed target states under the shared protection boundary. Apply only the selected supported action, preserve repeatability until a verified terminal outcome, and never rerun semantic edits.

how_much.scope: Current v3 transaction recovery, including initial creation with absent before-state. Retired, mixed, or unknown formats have no conversion or compatibility repair. The same observed external-editor race limit as publication applies; this does not provide historical-baseline restoration or an atomic guard against arbitrary outside edits.

acceptance_criteria: Before mutation, require the explicit transaction and expected-recovery identity to match a recognized current journal and verified exact snapshots. Missing, corrupt, tampered, unsupported, retired, or mixed recovery information returns the safe recovery stop without guessed repair, conversion, or cleanup of unrecognized state.

Use the same containment, selected-change target, identity, and supported-writer protections as publication. At each required observed target check, accept only the recorded before or candidate bytes or absence; a third state stops recovery without overwrite.

Complete publishes only the exact verified prepared candidate and requires the declared decision-basis inputs still to match. Restore uses only verified before bytes and leaves external read-set files untouched. Neither action reruns targeted operations against a new snapshot or manufactures a decision, origin, or approval.

A transaction whose journal records committed state permits completion/cleanup but not restoration of the before-state, including when the success response was lost and the caller never observed it. Restoring uncommitted initial creation removes only transaction-created files and empty transaction-created directories, preserving preexisting or externally added content.

Another interruption preserves available recovery information and allows a later explicitly selected attempt with the refreshed recovery identity. Cleanup of private snapshots occurs only after a verified terminal recovery outcome; these snapshots never become workflow evidence.

Return the established recovered outcome or the specific stop and remaining recovery state. Unknown identities remain unavailable, and neither a failure to observe a terminal outcome nor retired historical bytes authorizes a fallback repair.

sources.basis: Derived from SR-045 for the proposed MOD-011 responsibility. Allocates SR-045 exact recovery, foreign-content preservation, acknowledged-commit limits, interruption, and retirement outcomes to FUNC-047. AR-023 owns explicit public selection and non-recovery command dispatch. These criteria specify intended observations, not executed product evidence or an adoption of the REM authoring format by the CLI.
